questions.prompt: Which chart type is most appropriate to show the distribution of a single quantitative variable?
questions.explanation: A histogram displays the frequency of data points within value ranges, making it ideal for showing distribution.

questions.prompt: When reporting a change from 10% to 12% on a bar chart, which axis configuration could mislead viewers?
questions.explanation: A 0-100 scale makes the 2% change appear negligible, distorting perception of the actual change.

questions.prompt: Which color scheme best preserves data integrity for viewers with color vision deficiency?
questions.explanation: Grayscale is readable for all viewers, including those with color blindness, ensuring accurate data interpretation.

questions.prompt: What is an example of chartjunk?
questions.explanation: 3D effects add unnecessary visual complexity that can distract from the data.

questions.prompt: If you want to highlight a single outlier in a scatter plot, which technique is most appropriate?

options.text: Both increase size and change color

questions.explanation: Both size and color changes draw attention without altering the underlying data.

questions.prompt: Which practice is essential for honest data visualization?
questions.explanation: Accurately representing scales ensures viewers receive a truthful depiction of the data.
